chunks: And in the narration of al-Muthannā, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:
If the one who raised him seeks repayment for his maintenance, and he is financially capable, it is to be repaid to him. But if he is not financially capable, then what was spent is charity.

key_terms.الْمُثَنَّى: the narrator al-Muthannā in the sanad
key_terms.بِنَفَقَتِهِ: through spending on his maintenance and support
key_terms.رَبَّاهُ: raised him and took care of his upbringing
key_terms.رِوَايَةِ: narration or reported version of the hadith
key_terms.صَدَقَةً: charity, meaning the expenditure is counted as charitable giving
key_terms.مُوسِرًا: financially well-off or capable of paying

ai.seo_question: If someone raises a foundling, can they later demand repayment for the money they spent on him?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning reimbursement for the expenses of raising a foundling. If the person raised later has financial means, repayment may be sought from him; otherwise, the expenditure is treated as charity.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3532 - In the narration of Al-Muthanna, from Abu Abdullah (as):

"If the one who raised the abandoned child demands repayment for his expenses and he (the child) is financially capable, he must repay him. However, if he is not financially capable, then what was spent is considered charity."
